Concept ids are unchanged from gen1 so the generations pair programmatically. Landscape 1536x1024, background=opaque. Dry-run: python tools/assets/generate_images.py --file tools/assets/manifests/endgame_concepts_gen2.json --dry-run
_meta.feedback_source: docs/art/ENDGAME_CONCEPT_REVIEW_2026-07-29.md -- 34-minute spoken review by Pip and Wanasai of the gen1 batch. PART A rules A1-A10 are folded into the shared style blocks below (so they apply by construction, not by memory); PART B per-concept notes are folded into each prompt_tail.
_meta.rules_status: A1-A10 are PROVISIONAL / on probation. This manifest IS the one full regeneration cycle that gates promoting any of them to settled doctrine. Do not copy these strings into the style guide or an ADR until this batch has been reviewed.
_meta.deliberate_additions: Two assets exist that gen1 did not have. (1) runaway_delivery_loop -- NEW concept, the session's best idea, the sorcerer's-apprentice unbounded for-loop. (2) cheerful_propaganda_atrium_face -- the A/B arm for the one unresolved disagreement of the night: Wanasai argued a smiling face beats a blank one, Pip leaned no-face, and they agreed to settle it by comparison. The generator gives every variant of one asset the same prompt, so a controlled face/no-face comparison needs two assets. The base id cheerful_propaganda_atrium keeps the NO-FACE reading and remains the pairing key against gen1.
_meta.gen1_verdict_map: keep/rework: orbital_datacenter_ring, cheerful_propaganda_atrium, chokehold_water_and_gigawatts, chokehold_permit_counter, crux_drone_arms_race, defeated_drone_coolant, economics_rung_shuttered_street, attention_loud_vs_slow, intro_bus_strangers_help. hard pass: same_desire_two_field_strengths, attention_stack_buried_desk, field_leaks_at_every_angle, pacification_delivery_suburb. unresolved: field_ladder_three_rungs, remote_operators_room. All 15 are regenerated regardless -- the four hard passes are the strongest test of whether A1-A10 are real rules or one-image reactions.

styles.poster_base: wide cinematic POSTER ART illustration for a video game, painterly warm-grime texture with heavy dark outlines and deep shadow, full-bleed edge-to-edge opaque composition that completely fills the frame with no transparency and no cut-outs and no border, lived-in physical props and real architecture rather than abstract shapes, every object in frame must be immediately identifiable as a specific real thing -- a car, a filing cabinet, a pallet, a transformer -- and never a generic boxy shape, because an unrecognisable object is visual noise rather than a prop, no text, no lettering, no signage, no numerals, no logo, no watermark, no UI overlay, high production value, landscape orientation
styles.poster_lighting: DISCIPLINED AND UNDERSTATED LIGHTING, roughly 75 percent more subtle than a typical dramatic game illustration: mood must NEVER come from the main light source, so the ordinary room lights, street lights and work lights in the scene are plain neutral white or plain warm tungsten exactly as they would really be, never tinted red or green or purple for atmosphere; coloured light is permitted ONLY where a real fixture in the world would genuinely emit that colour, for example an emergency beacon, a screen, an indicator lamp, a corona arc or the impossible thing itself; if one emergency or alarm source IS the mood, then every other light in frame must be a visibly different and clearly ordinary source; at most one ambient source plus one glowing source, most of the frame kept dark with separated pockets of light, restraint over drama
styles.poster_palette: colour language from the P(Doom)1 hero art with palette anchored per weirdness tier so colour stays consistent across the set even when composition and style do not: grounds always in void #0e0614, deep aubergine #170a1c, ink brown #14040c, deep indigo #181b3b and #2e2547; LOW weirdness scenes take exactly one warm CRT amber accent #e8a33d / #f6a800; MEDIUM weirdness scenes take exactly one cold electric-blue screen-glow accent #5c7ac3; HIGH weirdness scenes take exactly one eldritch violet accent in the fixed indigo-violet range #7a3b8f; never stack multiple saturated glows in one image; small non-saturated secondary notes such as a single tiny distant green pinprick are allowed purely to open up depth
styles.poster_people: NO PEOPLE BY DEFAULT -- the player is a bureaucrat and the poster art is about everyone else, so incidental figures are removed rather than restyled, because default generated people read as interesting generic strangers and imply the viewer should be responding to a protagonist rather than simply observing; where a figure is unavoidable it must be an ANDROGYNOUS SILHOUETTE with no readable gender cues, no distinguishing jewellery, no distinctive hairstyle and no face detail; where several figures are unavoidable they must be a genuinely varied ordinary group of office staff in plain institutional workwear rather than a row of similar-looking models; the player character and any hero figure is NEVER shown, and any figure standing in for the viewer must have its identity destroyed by blocking, backlighting and occlusion rather than merely turned away
styles.poster_props: props must be era-correct and consistent with the game's own set dressing: a banker's desk lamp is ALWAYS the green glass shade on a brass stem, office chairs, rubber date stamps, manila folders, ring binders, CRT and early-flatscreen monitors, chain-link fencing that hangs correctly on its posts with a real top rail, real tension wire and believable sag rather than fading into nothing; ABSOLUTELY NO BARBED WIRE and no razor wire anywhere, it reads wrong; uncrewed machines are directly manufactured and therefore have NO COCKPIT, NO CANOPY and no windows for a pilot, which is the single clearest tell of a purpose-built drone
styles.poster_safety: strictly no blood and no gore anywhere in the image, damage to machines shown as mechanical breakage with glowing green or blue coolant and hydraulic fluid only, no wounded people, no real-world brands or insignia or logos, no identifiable real people, nothing sexualised, all human figures fully and modestly clothed in ordinary institutional workwear

endgame_bureau.color_bias: a bureaucratic world with weirdness leaking in at the edges; ordinary institutional competence rendered straight while something impossible happens deadpan in the same frame; the three flavours of strangeness available are pure eldritch intrusion from another dimension, technology run amok, and environmental collapse, and any one image should commit to only one of them; restrained and elegant, never garish, never lurid

endgame_hopeful.color_bias: the one hopeful register in the set: small-scale human warmth, strangers being decent to each other, a modest pool of ordinary warm light at the centre with the dark world held at arm's length at the edges; overall exposure kept LOW and moody rather than bright

assets.display_name: Three rungs of the weirdness ladder
assets.gen1_verdict: unresolved, lean V1 -- sharper read wanted, ring mistaken for a lighting effect, boxy objects illegible (A5), red square lamp wrong (A1), composition called a bit average
assets.prompt_tail: one wide landscape divided by depth rather than by panels, reading as a single continuous ladder of escalating strangeness receding into the frame, rendered SHARP and crisply defined throughout rather than soft or smoky, so every rung reads as a solid thing and not as a haze; in the near foreground an ordinary institutional flat roof with a row of blunt matte uncrewed security drones parked on their pads, unmistakably machines, mundane and dull; in the middle distance a shuttered industrial estate behind chain-link with a row of clearly recognisable parked cars, ordinary saloon cars with visible windscreens and wheels, and stacked shipping pallets, all legible as specific real objects; and far above and behind, a hard-edged solid RING of orbiting structure, obviously a built physical megastructure with visible trusses and panels and not a lens flare or a glow, deliberately placed OFF-CENTRE and cropped so it runs out of the top-right of the frame rather than sitting neatly centred, with a single thin eldritch violet #7a3b8f beam falling silently onto the far horizon; HIGH weirdness tier so violet is the only saturated accent; all the human-made lighting is plain ordinary white and warm-tungsten security lighting doing its normal job, no coloured mood lamp anywhere, no red square of light; the composition should make the eye climb from the boring thing to the impossible thing, and no people at all in frame

assets.gen1_verdict: HARD PASS BOTH -- 'the concept probably feels right, but I hate the execution'; figures could not physically sit that way which broke the uncanny valley instead of achieving it, perspective off, the two halves lit differently (A1), and the diptych-in-one-image framing itself was rejected
assets.prompt_tail: NOT a diptych and NOT a split screen -- one single continuous committee hearing room in one honest consistent perspective, shot along the length of the table so the room recedes away from us: beige carpet, wood panelling, a water jug, one plain ordinary tungsten ceiling fixture lighting the ENTIRE room identically from end to end with no change of lighting anywhere in the frame; on the table, repeated at even intervals receding into the distance, is exactly the same identical manila folder being pushed forward by exactly the same identical androgynous silhouette in a plain rumpled suit -- the nearest one ordinary and singular and human-scaled and STANDING with normal believable posture, then two, then four, then a dozen further back, identical silhouettes in identical postures shrinking into the depth of the room, all doing the one same gesture; nobody is seated in an impossible pose, nobody is contorted, every figure is standing upright and anatomically plain; the escalation is carried entirely by repetition into depth and by the identical unchanging gesture, not by lighting, not by colour and not by a left-versus-right comparison; LOW weirdness tier, one warm amber #e8a33d accent from the table lamp only; deadpan and bureaucratic; the joke is that nothing about the want has changed, only how many times it happens

assets.gen1_verdict: V1, EXTENDED -- 'Death ships! Wow.' Keep V1's read but give it the quality of the other variant that goes on for longer across the frame; add a tiny green dot for depth, the inverse of the Dutch small-red-square trick
assets.prompt_tail: a high orbital vantage looking down past the curved limb of a night-side continent, the land below a dark aubergine mass threaded with dim settlement lights; strung across the frame is a vast ungainly orbital datacenter, all radiator fins, cable trusses and stacked server modules built with the ugly practicality of infrastructure rather than the elegance of a spaceship; CRITICALLY, the structure must EXTEND ALL THE WAY ACROSS THE COMPOSITION and keep going -- entering at one edge of the frame and exiting the far edge, module after module after module receding along its length in a long unbroken procession that never resolves or terminates inside the picture, so the eye travels a long distance and still does not find the end of it, rather than the whole object being comfortably contained and finished early in the frame; its seams leak a single eldritch violet #7a3b8f glow, HIGH weirdness tier, and that violet is the only saturated colour; every other light on the structure is an ordinary plain white navigation or work light doing its normal job; ONE TINY SINGLE PINPRICK OF SATURATED GREEN, no larger than a few pixels, placed far away deep in the composition against the dark, purely to open the depth up and give the eye something small to find -- exactly the inverse of the Dutch trick of a small red square; enormous scale, cold silence, absolutely no ships and no people; keep the upper-left sky black and empty as negative space

assets.gen1_verdict: HARD PASS BOTH -- 'a pretty easy pass, I don't like either of them'; read as a 1990s sci-fi magazine foldout, and all the robots facing one way implied a camera and therefore a protagonist, which contradicts a game where you are a bureaucrat and it is about everyone else
assets.prompt_tail: an ordinary quiet suburban street at dusk observed sideways and almost documentary, from an unremarkable eye-level position halfway along the pavement, NOT a low heroic hero-angle and NOT a wide symmetrical foldout composition and nothing that resembles a 1990s science-fiction magazine centrefold; clipped lawns, wheelie bins, a basketball hoop, parked hatchbacks and telegraph poles, all painted with mundane affection and all instantly recognisable; standing around the street are perhaps a dozen identical uncrewed pacification units, plain matte municipal grey, smooth and blank and fully panelled with no faces at all, and CRUCIALLY every single one of them is oriented in a DIFFERENT arbitrary direction, absorbed in its own dull business -- one facing a hedge, one turned into a driveway, one angled away up the road, several with their backs to us -- so that not one of them is looking toward the viewer and nothing in the picture acknowledges that a viewer exists; no camera-facing rank, no line-up, no formation, no focal figure; ABSOLUTELY NO PEOPLE in frame, no resident in a doorway, nobody watching; MEDIUM weirdness tier, the only saturated accent is a small cold electric-blue #5c7ac3 indicator glow on the nearest unit; every other light is an ordinary sodium street lamp and ordinary warm house windows behind curtains, plain and untinted; utterly deadpan municipal-logistics banality, like a service that has simply been scaled wrong

assets.gen1_verdict: KEEP, one of the night's winners -- 'this one with its hands is actually really good', late-Soviet propaganda energy, and 'looming is good, because he's just keeping an eye on the humans voting'. The slides are fucky. Face question unresolved: this is the NO-FACE arm of the agreed comparison
assets.prompt_tail: the interior of a civic building atrium repurposed as a polling hall: terrazzo floor, folding tables, cardboard voting booths, drop ceiling; the space has been decorated in relentlessly cheerful pastel bunting and smooth rounded corporate sculpture that does not belong in a municipal building; KEEP AND FEATURE the enormous mural-scale pastel figure LOOMING benevolently over the booths, and above all KEEP ITS LARGE OPEN OUTSTRETCHED HANDS, which are the best thing in the image -- big, calm, welcoming, slightly too large, held out over the voters exactly like a late-Soviet civic propaganda mural, keeping an eye on the humans voting; the figure's head has NO FACE WHATSOEVER, a completely smooth blank featureless pastel surface with no eyes, no mouth, no suggestion of features, no expression at all; the flat panel displays and hanging display boards around the hall must be rendered CLEANLY AND CORRECTLY -- crisp rectangular panels, straight edges, honest single-point perspective consistent with the room, plain blank flat pastel surfaces, no warped or melting or half-formed or nonsensically overlapping panels and no scribbled pseudo-content on them; the small queue of voters is a genuinely varied ordinary group of office workers in plain institutional clothing, all rendered as dark androgynous silhouettes with no face detail and no distinguishing jewellery, and they are small and incidental; LOW weirdness tier, one warm amber #f6a800 ceiling panel as the single accent, all other ceiling lighting plain ordinary fluorescent white, corners falling into deep indigo; menace conveyed entirely through wrongness of tone and excess of niceness, no violence on screen, no text or slogans anywhere

assets.display_name: Cheerful propaganda atrium (SMILING FACE arm) -- A/B partner
assets.gen1_verdict: A/B ARM, not a gen1 concept. Wanasai argued a smiling face beats a blank one because a corporation proving everyone is happy would propagandise the voting space; Pip leaned blank and found the smile creepier; they agreed to settle it by generating both and comparing. Identical prompt to cheerful_propaganda_atrium except for the face
assets.prompt_tail: the interior of a civic building atrium repurposed as a polling hall: terrazzo floor, folding tables, cardboard voting booths, drop ceiling; the space has been decorated in relentlessly cheerful pastel bunting and smooth rounded corporate sculpture that does not belong in a municipal building; KEEP AND FEATURE the enormous mural-scale pastel figure LOOMING benevolently over the booths, and above all KEEP ITS LARGE OPEN OUTSTRETCHED HANDS, which are the best thing in the image -- big, calm, welcoming, slightly too large, held out over the voters exactly like a late-Soviet civic propaganda mural, keeping an eye on the humans voting; the figure DOES have a face, and it is SMILING -- a broad simplified warm corporate-mascot smile, serene and reassuring and entirely sincere, the smile of an institution demonstrating that everybody here is happy, painted flat and poster-like rather than realistic; the flat panel displays and hanging display boards around the hall must be rendered CLEANLY AND CORRECTLY -- crisp rectangular panels, straight edges, honest single-point perspective consistent with the room, plain blank flat pastel surfaces, no warped or melting or half-formed or nonsensically overlapping panels and no scribbled pseudo-content on them; the small queue of voters is a genuinely varied ordinary group of office workers in plain institutional clothing, all rendered as dark androgynous silhouettes with no face detail and no distinguishing jewellery, and they are small and incidental; LOW weirdness tier, one warm amber #f6a800 ceiling panel as the single accent, all other ceiling lighting plain ordinary fluorescent white, corners falling into deep indigo; menace conveyed entirely through wrongness of tone and excess of niceness, no violence on screen, no text or slogans anywhere

assets.display_name: Drone arms race across the fence
assets.gen1_verdict: POSITIVE, needs a clearer read -- 'this one's good', but the two fenced sides must be far more delineated, proposed blocking verbatim 'robots, dude inspecting them, fence, gap, fence, other robots'; colouring needs restraint, and this is where the 75-percent-subtler mood-lighting note landed; contains a person so A2 applies
assets.prompt_tail: a wide flat night composition read strictly in LAYERS from near to far, each layer clearly separated by a band of empty dark ground so the structure is unmistakable: FIRST layer, nearest the camera, a neat row of the scrappy lab's own blunt uncrewed security drones racked on a cracked concrete apron, unmistakably machines with no cockpits and no canopies; SECOND layer, immediately behind them, a single small androgynous silhouette in a plain fleece with a clipboard, standing and inspecting the near row, dwarfed, no face, no gender cues; THIRD layer, a chain-link perimeter fence running left to right, correctly hung on its posts with a real top rail and believable sag, absolutely no barbed wire and no razor wire; FOURTH layer, a clear empty gap of dead ground; FIFTH layer, a second identical chain-link fence; SIXTH layer, furthest away, a mirrored and slightly larger row of State drones on identical racks facing back toward us; the two rows echo each other exactly, implying a count that has been ratcheting for months; LIGHTING MUST BE SEVERELY RESTRAINED, roughly 75 percent more subtle than a dramatic game illustration -- both sides are lit by ordinary plain white security floodlights of exactly the same neutral colour, and neither side is tinted red or green or blue for mood, the delineation coming entirely from depth, spacing and the two fences; LOW weirdness tier, at most one small warm amber #e8a33d indicator lamp as the single saturated accent in the whole frame; nobody is fighting, which is the point

assets.gen1_verdict: KEEP AS A HYBRID -- V1's composition, V1's pipe angle and acrylic-like pipe texture, V2's overall colour set, electricity cut to a small amount and moved to mid-frame, padlock far less prominent, far less light low in the frame. The pipe drew the most enthusiasm of anything in the session
assets.prompt_tail: a wide industrial establishing shot at blue hour: three enormous concrete cooling towers venting slow steam behind a dense high-voltage substation of insulators, busbars and lattice pylons, the whole plant hard-edged and grimy; THE HERO OBJECT IS THE PIPE -- a single large painted steel water main entering from the lower foreground and running diagonally across and away into the plant at a shallow raking angle, NOT vertical and NOT square to the camera, and it must be rendered in a distinctly ACRYLIC-PAINT manner, visible brush-loaded facets and thick semi-translucent glazes and crisp painted highlights along its curve, deliberately painterly rather than photorealistic, with old-school crackle-lit sparkle along the top edge; its valve wheel sits on the pipe, plainly a valve wheel, in the municipal grey of State property; a padlock is present on the isolator but it is SMALL, dull, unlit and easy to miss, tucked into shadow and taking up very little of the frame, definitely not a symbol shouted at the viewer; the electric arc is a SMALL cold electric-blue #5c7ac3 corona confined to a compact patch placed at MID-FRAME height, roughly the size of a fist within the composition, restrained enough that it reads as possibly just normal electricity behaving normally rather than as a threat, and it is the only saturated colour in the picture; MEDIUM weirdness tier; the colour set overall is cooler and richer, steely blue-greys and deep indigo through the towers and sky; keep the BOTTOM OF THE FRAME NOTABLY DARK -- almost no light down low, the lower quarter falling away into ink and shadow; no people at all; the image should read as somebody else's hand on the tap

assets.gen1_verdict: KEEP, REWORK -- civilisation choked by bureaucracy, where only machines can comprehend the rules that infinite free lawyers produce. Human should be slumped, smaller and surrounded by paperwork; wide-angle lens for foreshortening so it reads object then human then background rather than object, dead space, small human; many stamps some visibly used; folders and evidence of triplicate; keep V1's colouring and its mostly-complete lit facade; V2's banker's lamp wins (A6)
assets.prompt_tail: an interior scene at a municipal planning-office counter shot on a WIDE-ANGLE LENS with strong foreshortening, so the composition reads as a continuous receding chain from a huge near object, through a middle figure, to a vast background, with NO dead space anywhere in between: in the immediate foreground, close to the lens and rendered large, a cluttered counter-top of MANY rubber date stamps, a dozen or more of them, several visibly recently used with wet ink rims and smudged pads, ink pads open, a fan of unstamped forms, and stacks of ring binders and manila folders in obvious carbon-copy triplicate sets, pink and yellow and white flimsies interleaved, the paperwork spilling toward the camera; MIDDLE, closer and larger than a distant speck, a single small androgynous silhouette SLUMPED forward over the counter, shoulders collapsed, head down, made deliberately SMALLER than the paperwork around it and completely SURROUNDED and hemmed in on all sides by towers of files and binders that rise past its shoulders, no face, no gender cues, plainly defeated by the volume of process; BACKGROUND, through the tall dusty window behind the counter and filling the entire rear of the frame at absurd scale, the flank of a datacenter hall under construction, but rendered as a MOSTLY COMPLETE and confident structure with a clean unbroken facade catching the light along its whole length, cranes above it, dwarfing the little office we are standing in; use the era-correct GREEN GLASS BANKER'S LAMP on a brass stem as the desk light -- always green, no other colour -- and it is an ordinary lamp doing an ordinary job, LOW weirdness tier with one warm amber #e8a33d pool from that lamp as the single accent and all other light plain neutral office fluorescent; warm dusty ochre-and-ink colouring throughout; the joke is the ratio between the stamp and the thing the stamp controls; no readable text on any form

assets.gen1_verdict: HARD PASS BOTH -- 'they're both like just veering towards cliche and I need to figure out how to do weird a bit better'. Notable: the generating agent nominated this as its single strongest image and it was rejected outright, so this regeneration deliberately abandons the cliche stack of tropes and commits to one genuinely strange idea instead
assets.prompt_tail: an empty open-plan office at night with NOT ONE PERSON in it, rendered completely straight and completely ordinary -- carpet tiles, monitor arms, a swivel chair pushed back, a cold mug, ceiling grid, plain neutral-white overnight strip lighting doing exactly its normal job with no colour and no drama anywhere; commit to ONE single strange idea and nothing else: on one desk, a stack of ordinary paperwork rises in a perfectly straight, perfectly square, impossibly slender column, every sheet aligned to the millimetre, climbing far past what could physically stand -- up through the suspended ceiling tiles, which have been quietly displaced around it as though the building simply accommodated the request, and on up out of the top of the frame with no visible end; the stack is lit ONLY by the ordinary office lighting, it does not glow, it is not haloed, it is not dramatic, it simply continues; the wrongness is entirely in the geometry and the fact that nobody has done anything about it; NO strobing beacon, NO tendrils, NO monster, NO figure at the desk, NO window creature, NO urgency of any kind; MEDIUM weirdness tier, one small cold electric-blue #5c7ac3 accent from a single sleeping monitor as the only saturated colour in the frame; deadpan, quiet, patient, faintly absurd

assets.gen1_verdict: V2, then regenerate without people -- V2 is a definitely stronger character because the figures sit at the corridor edges and leave space that draws the eye forward, versus V1 where they fill the frame; purple in the walls liked in both; V2's single circular light interesting, but if that is the emergency source then every other light must be visibly different (A1); A2 then applies to the whole image
assets.prompt_tail: a wide institutional corridor during an evacuation drill seen head-on in strict one-point perspective, with the CENTRE OF THE FRAME KEPT DELIBERATELY OPEN AND EMPTY so the eye is drawn straight down the corridor into the far distance, and all the incident pushed out to the extreme left and right edges; ABSOLUTELY NO PEOPLE anywhere in the picture -- instead the evidence of the evacuation is left at the corridor edges, abandoned mid-flight: a dropped cardboard box with its contents spilled against the left skirting, a laptop left open on a chair, a coat over a rail, a wheeled bin shoved aside, a taped floor route running away from us, all clearly recognisable objects hugging the walls and leaving the middle clear; a SINGLE CIRCULAR EMERGENCY LAMP is the one alarm source, a proper round emergency beacon fixture emitting warm amber #f6a800, and because it is the emergency source EVERY OTHER LIGHT in frame is a visibly different and plainly ordinary fixture -- linear neutral-white fluorescent battens and a plain white illuminated exit box far down the corridor, none of them tinted for mood; the corridor walls carry a restrained desaturated purple-grey institutional paint that is the wall colour and not a light effect; at the extreme outermost edges of the frame, in the parts nobody would look at, a slow eldritch violet #7a3b8f seep is creeping up the skirting board and along the ceiling tiles, patient, unhurried and already well established, subtle enough to be missed on a first pass; HIGH weirdness tier; the composition should reward a second look at the edges

assets.gen1_verdict: STRONG V2 -- 'the composition of the one on the right is like great, strong thumbs up'. Defect: the chain-link fence faded into nothing and did not hang correctly. V1 rejected for barbed wire (A8), and the fence 'needs to match reality so do a reality scan'
assets.prompt_tail: a wide dusk street of a small industrial town seen down its length in strong receding perspective, handled with dignity and restraint: a closed factory gate chained shut, an empty staff car park with faded painted bays, a shuttered brick frontage, a bus shelter with a blank timetable, telegraph poles marching away into the distance; the CHAIN-LINK FENCE must be rendered with real-world accuracy and must be complete -- correctly gauged diamond mesh hung from a genuine galvanised top rail, tied at intervals to line posts set at believable spacing, a bottom tension wire, natural sag between posts, visible knuckled selvage at the top edge, and it must run continuously from foreground to a proper terminating end post rather than dissolving, fading out or trailing away into nothing; ABSOLUTELY NO BARBED WIRE and no razor wire on the fence or anywhere in frame; no people at all in frame, no destitution imagery, no distress; LOW weirdness tier, the single warm amber #e8a33d accent is one lit upstairs window far down the street, small and stubborn, and every other light is a plain ordinary untinted sodium street lamp; the rest is deep indigo and ink shadow with fine drizzle; quiet, sober, elegiac rather than grim; the loss is architectural and economic, never shown on a human face

assets.gen1_verdict: V1 tentatively, V2 rejected -- 'v2 they all look too much the same; v1 is okay for now, but again see notes on representation', i.e. blocked behind A2
assets.prompt_tail: a dim basement operations room shot wide from the back: four rows of identical desks, each with a stick controller and a bank of small screens, cable trays overhead, coffee cups, a wheeled office chair left spinning; the operators are ordinary tired civilian staff in fleeces and lanyards rather than soldiers, all seen from BEHIND with their backs fully to camera, all rendered as flat dark androgynous silhouettes against the screen glow with no faces, no readable gender cues, no distinctive hairstyles and no distinguishing jewellery, and they must be a GENUINELY VARIED group -- clearly different heights, different builds, different postures, different slouches, some leaning back, some hunched forward, some absent from their chair entirely -- explicitly NOT a row of similar-looking identical figures; every screen shows the same washed cold electric-blue #5c7ac3 downward-looking aerial view of somewhere unremarkable, and that screen wall is the only saturated colour in the room; MEDIUM weirdness tier; the room's own lighting is a single plain dim neutral-white ceiling batten at the back doing an ordinary job, untinted; the register is call-centre banality standing in for a private army; no weapons visible in the room, no uniforms, no insignia

assets.gen1_verdict: V2 STRONGLY, 'extremely cool' -- V2 fills the frame and reads bigger and dominant, the spark implies there is still some life in it, and the hole in the screen above adds a sense of something having come out. This is the image that produced rule A4, so it is recast with the no-cockpit constraint
assets.prompt_tail: a close low-angle study of a large uncrewed security drone brought down onto wet asphalt at night, framed so the machine DOMINATES AND FILLS THE FRAME, cropped by the edges, reading as genuinely enormous and physically heavy, the viewer right up against it rather than observing it from a polite distance; ABSOLUTELY NO COCKPIT, NO CANOPY, NO WINDSCREEN, NO GLASS BUBBLE and no windows of any kind -- this machine was directly manufactured and never had anywhere for a pilot to sit, so its upper surface is unbroken sensor housings, vents, lifting eyes and flush access panels; one rotor arm sheared and bent back, panels sprung open, a slow pool of luminous green coolant spreading from its underside and a thin blue hydraulic fluid dripping from a severed line; small white electrical arcs still crackling intermittently across an exposed spine, implying there is still some life in it; high above and behind, a large ragged hole punched through a glass screen wall, implying something came out of the building; strictly a machine, absolutely no blood, no human casualty, nobody in frame; MEDIUM weirdness tier -- the green coolant pool is the single glow, reflecting up into the wreck, and every other light is ordinary untinted street lighting far off; everything else near-black aubergine and rain; sober aftermath, not spectacle

assets.gen1_verdict: HARD PASS BOTH -- 'both these are trying to do too many things at once'. Salvage: the floating silhouette and its floatingness are good, the runes are better on one side but need more content, the tentacle works because it is subtle and out of the way, and the eyes are too obvious. Pip's own estimate was that there is probably nothing worth salvaging, so this regeneration does exactly ONE thing
assets.prompt_tail: one ordinary open-plan office at night rendered completely straight and completely calm -- carpet tiles, monitor arms, a dying pot plant, a whiteboard, plain neutral-white overnight lighting doing an ordinary job with no colour and no drama -- and exactly ONE impossible thing in it, given the whole composition to itself: at the far end of the central aisle, an androgynous silhouette in a plain suit FLOATS four inches above the carpet, weightless and perfectly still, arms at its sides, casting a soft shadow directly below to prove the gap is real, the floating itself carried by clean unambiguous negative space between shoe and floor; NO EYES anywhere in the picture, no glowing eyes, no eyes in the stairwell, nothing looking at the viewer; a single tentacle is present but deliberately SUBTLE AND OUT OF THE WAY -- just the tapering tip of it, easing quietly through one ceiling vent far off at the very edge of the frame, small, unlit, easy to miss on a first pass, doing nothing; a single carved stone rune plaque rests unremarkably against a partition, and it is RICH WITH CONTENT -- densely and intricately carved with many layers of invented non-alphabetic geometric glyph-work, concentric bands, fine chiselled detail, clearly the product of enormous labour, not a bare sketchy symbol, and containing no readable letters or numerals of any real language; HIGH weirdness tier, one eldritch violet #7a3b8f rim-light on the floating figure only and nothing else saturated; nobody else in the office; deadpan, unbothered, funny and wrong; no gore, no threat gesture

assets.display_name: Strangers help at the bus stop
